title: Nawazuddin Siddiqui's 'Dr. Hassan' Brings 'House' to India, Premieres December 11 on JioHotstar
excerpt: JioHotstar has released the teaser for its Hindi adaptation of the Hugh Laurie medical drama, with Dia Mirza as the hospital chief and Rohan Sippy directing.
body:
• Dr. Hassan, JioHotstar's Hindi adaptation of the American medical drama House, premieres on December 11, with Nawazuddin Siddiqui as the brilliant, difficult diagnostician.
  • Dia Mirza co-stars as the head of the hospital; Rohan Sippy directs and Banijay Asia produces, under licence from NBCUniversal Formats.
  • It is the third international adaptation of House, after versions in Russia and Turkey, according to NBCUniversal Formats.
  • The series streams exclusively on JioHotstar in India from December 11; the episode count has not been announced.

JioHotstar has released the teaser of Dr. Hassan, its Indian adaptation of House, and set the premiere for December 11. Nawazuddin Siddiqui plays the title role: a doctor whose diagnostic instincts crack cases that leave the rest of his team stumped, and whose temperament, as the teaser makes clear, is considerably harder to treat. The Hindi-language series is commissioned by JioHotstar and produced by Banijay Asia, with the format licensed by NBCUniversal Formats.

The cast and the character

Dia Mirza leads alongside Siddiqui as the head of the hospital — the role based on Dr. Cuddy in the original — and the teaser shows Hassan sporting House's trademark limp, clashing with patients, fellow doctors and Mirza's character. Rohan Sippy directs. The cast also includes Faisal Rashid, Rehmat Rattan, Jayson Thaam and Smaran Sanu. Vinay Chhawal and Ketan Pedgaonkar adapted and scripted the series, with dialogues by Virat Basoya.

Siddiqui said memories of his hometown shaped his approach to the role. "Growing up, I remember spending time around clinics and dispensaries in my hometown, and there were always such interesting people and situations unfolding there," he said. "What I enjoyed about playing him was finding the balance between his exceptional intelligence and his very particular way of looking at the world."

An Indian telling, not a transplant

Alok Jain, who heads JioStar's Hindi and English entertainment business, said the team started from a single question: what would this story look like if it were born in India? "Great characters travel, but they truly come alive when they are rooted in the world of the audience watching them," Jain said. "House gave the world one of television's most unforgettable characters, and with Dr. Hassan, we wanted to reimagine that spirit through an Indian lens, with its own humour and humanity." The series keeps the format's central premise — complex medical cases, unpicked week by week — while placing its characters, settings and conversations in an Indian context.

Deepak Dhar, founder and CEO of Banijay Asia and Endemol Shine India, said the adaptation was approached with care because the original is so widely loved. "At its heart is a truly singular character: sharp, flawed, often difficult, and impossible to ignore," Dhar said. Linfield Ng, VP of format sales and production at NBCUniversal Formats, noted that Dr. Hassan is the third international adaptation of the House format, after versions in Russia and Turkey.

The original it has to live up to

House, created by David Shore and produced by Universal Television, starred Hugh Laurie as Dr. Gregory House and ran on Fox for eight seasons, from 2004 to 2012. It won five Primetime Emmy Awards, two Golden Globe Awards, a Peabody Award and nine People's Choice Awards. Dr. Hassan joins Banijay Asia's existing format adaptations on the platform, including The Night Manager and Mistry, the Indian version of Monk.

How to watch

Dr. Hassan premieres on December 11, exclusively on JioHotstar in India. The streamer has not announced an episode count. For viewers outside India, no separate international release has been announced; the December 11 date is the JioHotstar premiere.
